title: A novel deep neural network model based Xception and genetic algorithm for detection of COVID-19 from X-ray images.
summary: The study optimized an Xception CNN with a genetic algorithm for COVID-19 classification on chest radiographs and reported held-out diagnostic performance on 277 images from a public 1,251-image collection. The study-specific task and test-set comparison support a retrospective diagnostic-validation result; they do not establish external clinical performance or patient benefit.
ai_technology: A genetic algorithm searches Xception CNN architecture/hyperparameters for classification of COVID-19, viral pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia and normal X-rays.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: For the public 1,251-image dataset (974 train/277 test), the paper reports accuracy .996 for binary, .989 for three-class and .924 for four-class classification, compared with cited prior models.
evidence.unknown: The 277-image held-out set includes 60 COVID-19 images and is compared with image labels/model baselines. This is retrospective validation on a public dataset, without external-site or prospective clinical evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: A genetic algorithm searches Xception CNN architecture/hyperparameters for classification of COVID-19, viral pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia and normal X-rays.
